title: Cozy Cole's 24-inch cymbal and big bass drums
summary: Cole gave him a 24-inch crash cymbal; Moore recalls huge bass drums, Zutty Singleton's and the show drummer Battleaxe's pedal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: And they had some very good drummers during that time, very good. Cozy Cole was a great tom-tom man. He loved to play tom-toms. He liked to play cymbals, too. In fact, he gave me a cymbal that was too large for him because he...
He gave me a cymbal which was a 24-inch cymbal.

24-inch. It was one of them old-time crash cymbals. There wasn't no rivets in it. You got to hit it very hard to get a sound out of it because it's so large. It was too heavy to really take around. Because during that time, I think they were using around a 24-inch bass drum. They don't use that size very much no more now. They're using 18-inch, 22-inch... That's about the standard, 18" and 20" and 22". Some of them still use 24". When I first come to New York, I had a 28-inch bass drum, one of them great
big bass drums. They don't use them no more. Take up too much... It's too loud. Take up too much room on the bandstand.
28 inches, that's a huge... That's like the ones that you carry in front of you in a marching band.

Yes. And during that time, Zutty Singleton, he was using a 28-inch. This drummer that I met, he was a great show drummer, playing shows -- his name was Battleaxe. He used an overhead pedal. The pedal was round and it fastened on the top of the bass drum. He would beat it (?). Something like the alligator foot pedal.
It would be something like that. He would use a big piece of plank, a board the size of...the length of your foot. They can't... They don't like them cymbals no more.
